modelingNotes: Camp North End: the Raceway Building — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-cne-raceway-building.ts

The long, low brick building on the Ford plant's parcel between the Boileryard and Hercules South (`clt-cne-hercules-south.ts`), 1824 Statesville Avenue, Suite 100; Camp North End's "Raceway Bldg" (17,000 sq ft), now small shops and a bar along The Raceway. It stands on the edge of the old rail yard: its south front is a single storey at the level of the Boileryard, its north side drops some four metres to the tracks' level, where it had loading doors on a raised dock. Four roof lengths at slightly different heights, a white membrane roof with a short overhang on the south.

Evidence: - OSM: way/324611745 (height 5, named "Camp North End Boileryard Building" in OSM; the brochure and the county address name it the Raceway Building). The shops mapped along its south face (Canteen, Thrift Pony, Wily, galleries) are nodes, not parts. - Lidar, USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016, 1 m (measured, NAVD88): ground 224.7–225.1 along the south front, 220.7–220.9 on the north (the rail level; y = 0 is 220.8), with an earth bank rising to 224.7 against the north wall's middle third; roofs, west to east, 229.8 (x −70…−54, parapet 230.2), 229.3 (−54…−14), 230.4 (−14…34), 229.6 (34…67); the roof reaching about 1.7 m past the OSM south wall at 230.3–230.9. - Mecklenburg County tax parcel 07903105 (the Ford parcel): improvements dated 1924, 1939 and 1956, face brick, one storey; which date is this building's is not recorded. - Camp North End leasing brochures (2021, 2023, camp.nc): "Raceway Building 17,000 sq ft"; the 2023 site rendering places "Raceway Bldg" here (look-only; name only). - USGS NAIP orthophoto (public domain): the white roof and its steps.

No licensed photo was found (Commons, Openverse, Mapillary). Estimated: the brick (the campus Kahn brick), the shopfront bays (one glazed bay per 6.1 m between brick piers, sill at the south grade), the north loading doors (one per 12.2 m where the wall stands clear of the bank), the overhang's depth. Invented: the high window over each north door and the window pairs in the end walls. The building's date and original use are unknown; it is modelled as it stands.
Frame: the Ford plant's grid (`clt-cne-hercules-south.ts`); placement bearing 6.3. The origin is the outline's centroid, lng −80.8327406, lat 35.2476582.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-cne-raceway-building", model "clt-cne-raceway-building"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-cne-raceway-building.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
